title: D. Almost Roman
statement:
Let's define a value of a string, consisting of letters " XVI ", as follows:

You are given a string of characters " XVI? " and asked $$q$$ queries about it.

In the $$i$$-th query, three integers are provided:

What is the minimum value of the string that can be obtained if all question marks are replaced with the letters ' X ', ' V ', ' I ' so that the number of used letters does not exceed the number of available letters of each type?

The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $$n$$ and $$q$$ ($$1 $\leq n, q \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the string and the number of queries, respectively.

The second line contains a string consisting of $$n$$ characters ' X ', ' V ', ' I ' and/or ' ? '.

The $$i$$-th of the following $$q$$ lines contains three integers $$c_X, c_V$$, and $$c_I$$ ($$0 $\leq c_X, c_V, c_I \leq n$$$) — the number of available letters ' X ', ' V ' and ' I ' in the $$i$$-th query.

Additional constraints on the input:

For each query, print a single integer — the minimum value of the string that can be obtained by replacing all question marks with the available letters ' X ', ' V ', and/or ' I '.
input: Input The first line contains one integer $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$n$$ and $$q$$ ($$1 $\leq n, q \leq 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the string and the number of queries, respectively. The second line contains a string consisting of $$n$$ characters ' X ', ' V ', ' I ' and/or ' ? '. The $$i$$-th of the following $$q$$ lines contains three integers $$c_X, c_V$$, and $$c_I$$ ($$0 $\leq c_X, c_V, c_I \leq n$$$) — the number of available letters ' X ', ' V ' and ' I ' in the $$i$$-th query. Additional constraints on the input: the sum of $$n$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$3 $\cdot 10^5$$$; the sum of $$q$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$3 $\cdot 10^5$$$; $$c_X + c_V + c_I$$ is greater than or equal to the number of ' ? ' characters in the given string.
output: Output For each query, print a single integer — the minimum value of the string that can be obtained by replacing all question marks with the available letters ' X ', ' V ', and/or ' I '.
